sections.h2: Fastest ways to sell in Waco
sections.html:
The quickest Waco sales are direct purchases: the buyer pays cash, takes the house in its present shape and closes once title work is complete. A retail listing can reach more buyers, but showings, inspections and lender approval stretch the calendar.

Nearly half of Waco's housing is renter-occupied, so many houses here are held as rentals. If yours has a tenant, share the lease terms early, since they decide when a buyer can take possession.

  • Fast route: cash buyer, short inspection period and a closing date you pick.
  • Open-market route: staging, showings and a buyer whose loan must be approved.
  • Slow route: unresolved liens, an open estate or a tenant who will not leave.

Waco lies in central McLennan County, about seventy miles south of Dallas, near where the Brazos and Bosque rivers join. Interstate 35, U.S. highways 84 and 77 and State Highway 6 are the main roads. Baylor University has been here since 1887, and the city mixes older central blocks with newer outer neighborhoods.

When you describe a house to a buyer, tie it to a part of town: the older core, the Baylor area or a newer outer street. That helps a buyer place it quickly. Ask your title company how long a typical Waco closing takes so you can plan a move around it.

A typical owned Waco home is valued at $221,700 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and only 49.4 percent of units are owner-occupied. That split explains why investors are a visible part of the market.

About 79.1 percent of residents were at the same address a year earlier, so roughly one in five had moved. The city covers 88.73 square miles of land with an average trip to work of 18.7 minutes, and a short commute is worth naming in a listing.

With rents near $1,165 a month, a rental-minded buyer will test an offer against that figure. Have the lease, deposit records and repair invoices ready.

An investor looking at a Waco rental will usually care about three things: the rent the house can command, the cost of getting it ready for the next tenant, and how soon the keys change hands. A house with a tenant already paying on time can be more attractive to that buyer, not less. A vacant house with deferred repairs can still sell, just at a price that reflects the work.

Unpaid property tax is secured by a lien, and paying back taxes on a property does not make someone its owner. Tax sales are the final remedy, and the City of Waco says they may occur on the first Tuesday of any month.

  • The McLennan County Tax Office conducts its tax sales online through GovEase, so confirm the current format with the office.
  • A property drawing no bid within city limits is struck off to the City of Waco, which resells it after a six-month or two-year redemption period.
  • Property without a homestead exemption can be bought back within six months by paying 25 percent of the auction price plus taxes, costs and fees.
  • Homestead or special-use property has two years, at 25 percent in the first year and 50 percent in the second.

Taxes are due on receipt of the bill and are delinquent if not paid before February 1. Online payments carry a 2.19 percent card fee or a $1.50 flat electronic check fee.

Deeds for Waco property are filed with the McLennan County Clerk after a notary acknowledgment. Ask that office for the full recording charge on your document.

For an inherited house, an affidavit of heirship has no court review behind it, and no law forces a title company to accept it. If a tenant will not leave, a justice court case follows written notice, and a writ of possession cannot issue until six days after judgment.

For homestead owners, school districts must give a $140,000 exemption, and a veteran rated 100 percent disabled can receive a total exemption on the homestead.

sections.h2: City offices for zoning and building questions
sections.html:
Calling the right desk first saves a week of phone tag. Fix-ups, additions and demolitions can all raise questions that only the city can answer, so a short call before you commit to work is time well spent.

  • Zoning and setback questions: Planning Services Division, (254) 750-5650.
  • What may be built on a lot: Inspection Services and Plan Review, (254) 750-5674.
  • Water and sewer access: Engineering Department, (254) 750-5440.
  • Affordable housing programs: Housing and Community Development Services, (254) 750-5656.

A buyer using housing assistance may have a timeline of their own, so ask early. The city sells tax-foreclosed properties by sealed bid, and most are sold at the courthouse auctions through a law firm. A seller whose house might otherwise end up there has far more control by selling before a tax sale takes place.

sections.h2: What to prepare before you sell
sections.html:
Collect the deed, your loan payoff, the latest tax bill and any lease. If repairs were done, add the invoices. A title company can then check for liens and tell you how quickly it can close.

If the house has a mortgage, request a written payoff that stays good through your target closing date. If it has none, ask the title company to confirm that no old lien remains on the record. Old liens from contractors or past owners are easy to miss, and they are far cheaper to clear before an offer than during the final week.

On the day itself, bring a photo ID, hand over all keys and openers, and schedule your utility shutoff. Expect the signing itself to take under an hour, with the notary confirming each signature before the deed goes to the McLennan County Clerk. A cash sale keeps this part simple: no appraisal visit, no loan underwriter, and a closing date set by the title work and your own plans. If a delay does come up, it is usually a missing signature from a co-owner or an unresolved lien, so find out early who else is on the deed and whether anyone must sign with you.

faqs.q: When are Waco tax sales held?
faqs.a: The City of Waco says tax sales may occur on the first Tuesday of any month, while the McLennan County Tax Office conducts its sales online through GovEase. Confirm the format with the tax office.

faqs.q: Can a former owner reclaim a Waco house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Property without a homestead exemption can be bought back within six months at 25 percent of the auction price plus costs, and homestead or special-use property has two years at 25 or 50 percent.

faqs.q: Does a tenant slow a Waco sale?
faqs.a: It can. A buyer needs the lease term and any deposit records. If the tenant must leave, the case runs through justice court after written notice.

faqs.q: Who do I ask about the tax balance on my Waco house?
faqs.a: The McLennan County Tax Office, which also sets out the due-date rules and payment options. The appraisal district sets value but does not collect.

faqs.q: How is ownership of an inherited Waco house documented?
faqs.a: Through probate or a court-backed route, or by a transfer on death deed filed before the owner died. A sworn heirship statement may not satisfy a buyer.
